headlines.title: Community advocates concerned after ICE agents spotted at Milpitas jail
headlines.description: Community advocates raised concerns about ICE activity at a South Bay jail. Cellphone video obtained by NBC Bay Area shows armed federal immigration agents both inside and outside the Elmwood Correctional Facility in Milpitas. Advocates with Silicon Valley De-Bug and the Santa Clara County Rapid Response Network were at the facility, raising questions about why agents were there and whether their activity conflicts with the county’s sanctuary policy. “It is deeply concerning. This feels like a recent escalation, and we don’t know if it’s the beginning of a larger operation or what’s motivating it,” Raj Jayadev with Silicon Valley De-Bug said. “They were here yesterday so we were ready, Rapid Response Network was out here as well.” Raj Jayadev says both Silicon Valley De-Bug and the Rapid Response Network are concerned that the agents are waiting to pick up people, just as they’re being released. “We had seen people and known people that were being released from jail and they never made it home because ICE was waiting for them to pick them up,” Jayadev said. The sheriff’s office says the agents did not make any arrests or detainments Thursday and remained in areas open to the public. Advocates say they believe ICE’s presence conflicts with the county’s civil immigration policy, which generally prohibits county staff from helping with federal civil immigration enforcement, including sharing release dates. “I think our concerns are to make sure the sheriffs in the county are not participating in anything that ICE wants to do,” Narely Campos with Silicon Valley De-Bug said. It’s worth noting that no sanctuary policy can prohibit the agents from waiting inside or outside public areas of the jail. In a statement, the sheriff’s office reiterated that it does not coordinate with ICE, notify the agency of release dates or have advance knowledge of its operations. The office says ICE has periodically visited the jail’s lobby for more than a year and has taken 60 people into custody who were scheduled for release. The sheriff’s office says there were no incidents reported and jail operations continued as normal.

headlines.title: San Francisco house allegedly occupied by squatters to go up for auction
headlines.description: In one of San Francisco’s most exclusive neighborhoods, a house that neighbors claim is occupied by squatters will go up for auction soon. The four-bedroom house on 32nd Avenue in the Sea Cliff neighborhood seems to fit right in on the upscale street, but neighbors say squatters have been a persistent problem. “It’s quiet right now in the middle of the day when they’re not here, but if you came between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m., you’d be hearing dogs barking all night, car doors slamming,” resident Cameron Will said. “There were enormous thuds last night keeping neighbors up. That’s very common. I’d say that’s probably five out of seven days a week.” Will said the ongoing nuisance has resulted in neighbors resorting to documenting everyone who comes and goes. Will said they’ve counted up to three dozen people over the last two months. No one answered the door when an NBC Bay Area crew knocked Thursday. The San Francisco Board of Supervisors this week authorized the city to put the house on auction due to years of unpaid property taxes that now total about $340,000. The city attorney also has filed a lawsuit against Diana Peng, Brandon Aadee and several unnamed people, alleging Peng and Aadee are conspiring to illegally gain title of the house. The special auction will likely be set for December. According to online real estate estimates, it could be worth upwards of $4 million. But if someone produces a valid title and is able to pay the tax bill, the whole plan could be derailed, along with neighbors’ hopes of finding some peace on their street.

headlines.title: How a dual language program is helping a struggling San Jose school district
headlines.description: A San Jose school district is considering reopening a campus it previously closed thanks to a successful dual language immersion program. Declining enrollment has school districts across California, including San Jose’s Alum Rock Union Elementary School District (ARUSD), facing the prospect of closing schools. ARUSD’s Ben Painter Elementary School was on the list of schools slated to potentially close due to low enrollment, but demand for its Vietnamese dual language immersion program ballooned this fall. “This year we have every classroom full,” Painter Elementary Principal Dr. Joseph Manluco said. “We have kids in every classroom with a large and growing Vietnamese dual language immersion program.” There are 420 students at Painter Elementary, a number that might bode well for other campuses that are currently shut down. “We do have other campuses within the district that are exceeding enrollment, where they need more room,” ARUSD Superintendent Dr. Marnie Hazelton said. “We are working with committees along with our board members and a local real estate agency to see if it is a viable option to reopen some of these campuses.” Pew Research estimates San Jose has the largest population of Vietnamese people outside of Vietnam at roughly 150,000. Painter Elementary’s program is the second largest Vietnamese dual language immersion program in Northern California. The idea is to combine quality academics with a second language. But there are plenty of non-Vietnamese American students on campus. “We have students in here that are becoming trilingual or even quadrilingual,” Manluco said.

headlines.title: WNBA Finals: Valks look to even series vs. Dream after dropping back-to-back games
headlines.description: The Golden State Valkyries will look to stop the surging Atlanta Dream in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals. A win for the Valks at Saturday’s game in Atlanta would even the best-of-seven series at 2-2. A loss would put Golden State on the brink of elimination and give Atlanta its first title. Game 4 comes after the Dream won back-to-back games against the Valkyries, who won the series opener. How to watch Valkyries vs. Dream in the WNBA Finals The series will air across NBC and USA Network. Game 4 will be on NBC Bay Area. All games can also be streamed on Peacock. headlines.title: Highway 37 in North Bay to close this weekend for El Niño storm preps
headlines.description: Highway 37 in the North Bay will shut down in both directions this weekend to allow Caltrans crews time to raise the flood-prone area ahead of a potentially powerful El Niño and winter storms. Motorists traveling through the area should expect significant delays and increased travel times. Here’s what to know about the closure and detour information. When will Highway 37 shut down? The closure on the highway starts at 10 p.m. Friday. Caltrans expects to reopen lanes by 5 a.m. Monday. What part of Highway 37 will close during weekend closure? Highway 37 will shut down between Mare Island in Vallejo and Sears Point in Sonoma County, according to Caltrans. Detour information for Highway 37 closure Motorists traveling on eastbound Highway 37 during the closure will exit left onto northbound Highway 121 in Sonoma; Make a right on Highway 12, 1(Carneros Hwy) and continue; Right on Highway 12/Highway 29; Enter left for the connector loop off-ramp back to eastbound Highway 37. Motorists traveling on westbound Highway 37 will exit right onto northbound Highway 29 in Napa, and follow Highway 29 to westbound Highway 12, then to southbound Highway 121; Why is Caltrans shutting down Highway 37? Highway 37 near Mare Island has flooded repeatedly over the years. Caltrans said the work is designed to help reduce flooding risks on the vital commuter route. headlines.title: Pacifica Pier repairs cause traffic headaches
headlines.description: Major repairs at the Pacifica Pier are causing traffic headaches for people in the area. A large crane and other heavy equipment have rolled in along Beach Boulevard Thursday, which will be used to stabilize the cracked pier. “Right now there is a void there and wave will continue to wash away, and we want to make sure we protect the street and the utilities and the residences in the neighborhood,” Pacifica City Manager Sean Charpentier said. It could take crews up to five days to position the crane, while the overall repair phase is expected to last at least three months. The pier has been closed since June, when engineers discovered major cracking. The city says it’s moving as quickly as possible to create this “temporary fix” due to the expected record-breaking storm season. “So, this does not fix the pier, this just helps to shore it up to protect it though the winter,” Charpentier said. Residents are being warned to expect noise, and the city says parking could temporarily be affected. The city also says it’s still evaluating longer term repair options.

headlines.title: Preliminary 3.0 magnitude earthquake strikes near Hollister
headlines.description: A preliminary 3.0 magnitude earthquake struck near Hollister, according to the United States Geological Survey. The quake hit at 2:58 p.m. and was centered 14.6 miles south-southeast of Hollister, the USGS said. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates. headlines.title: Oakland's 911 system goes down, calls routed to Alameda County
headlines.description: All 911 calls in Oakland are being transferred to the Alameda County Sheriff’s Office. Oakland Police Department (OPD) dispatchers noticed that their computer systems started freezing around 8:30 p.m. Wednesday. Dispatchers tried both emergency and non-emergency lines and discovered there was no service to phone lines and internet. OPD dispatchers were moved to the Oakland Fire and Alameda County Sheriff’s dispatch center. Oakland police said they are only responding to priority one calls – such as active shootings, violent assaults and armed robberies – as the IT department looks to restore services with AT&T. The fire department is responding to fires and medical emergencies. The City of Oakland said its MACRO community response teams are available daily from 6:30 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. to help with non-emergency, non-violent situations. MACRO can be contacted at 510-446-2276. The city said MACRO is not a replacement for 911. AT&T said that a fiber optic cable was cut. They don’t believe it was theft or vandalism. AT&T also said calls are going through, but some calls are going to the wrong location. Oakland Police Department’s 911 Center is one of the busiest in California. It can get thousands of calls a day. It’s also been one of the most troubled 911 centers, dealing with some of the longest 911 answering times for years. But recently, it has seen major improvements and faster responses. So, short-term, this outage is impacting on anyone calling with an emergency where someone’s life isn’t immediately threatened. In the long term, this could impact the public’s trust in Oakland’s 911 system, that just started having reason to rebound.

headlines.title: FBI agent returns to the stand in Sheng Thao corruption trial
headlines.description: An FBI agent was back on the stand Thursday in the federal corruption trial of former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao, laying out evidence prosecutors say connects Thao and her co-defendants to a bribery and wire fraud scheme. Thao, her longtime partner Andre Jones, and businessmen David and Andy Duong are accused of conspiracy, bribery and wire fraud. Thursday marked the second day of testimony for FBI Special Agent Kathrine Barclay. Prosecutors outlined digital and financial evidence they believe directly connects the dots between the defendants and a fraud scheme. Prosecutors said phone records show Thao and Jones communicated with businessman Mario Juarez on the same day Juarez requested negative campaign mailers targeting Thao’s mayoral opponent, Loren Taylor. Barclay also testified that texts between Juarez and Andy Duong included drafts of the mailers and Juarez confirming he bought the website called taylorfraud.com. Barclay also pointed to a financial trail showing California Waste Solutions, which is owned by the Duong family, paid Juarez $75,000, the amount linked to the mailer campaign. Sheng Thao Oct 15 Sheng Thao Oct 19 Sheng Thao Oct 13 Text messages also appear to outline what prosecutors say was the broader deal: cash and help getting Thao elected in exchange for 300 modular housing units, a 10-year city contract extension for California Waste Solutions, and influence over city department appointments. In one message, Juarez described those terms to Andy Duong, who responded that nothing was missing. In another message, Andy Duong told Juarez, “Aint nothing free or front cuz we did all that to help her win.” Prosecutors said digital data from Andy Duong’s phone includes pictures and video showing meetings with Thao and the Duongs, a speech by Juarez celebrating the alleged deal, and photos of the alleged agreement. Thao, Jones and the Duongs have pleaded not guilty to conspiracy, bribery and wire fraud charges. Thursday ended with prosecutors still questioning Barclay. Defense attorneys are expected to get a chance to cross-examine her on Friday.

headlines.title: Westbound I-80 in San Francisco near the Bay Bridge to close this weekend
headlines.description: A section of westbound Interstate 80 in San Francisco near the Bay Bridge will be closed this weekend for a construction project. The full westbound I-80 closure from Fifth Street to 15th Street is scheduled to start at 11 p.m. Friday and continue until 6 a.m. Monday, according to Caltrans. Motorists should avoid using the Bay Bridge to get into San Francisco during the closure, Caltrans said. Alternate options include taking public transportation or using the San Mateo, Dumbarton or Richmond-San Rafael bridges. “This work is necessary for crews to place polyester concrete on the WB I-80 Bayshore freeway deck and will complete a broader I-80 Bayshore Freeway viaduct polyester concrete placement project which began on the eastbound I-80 Bayshore Freeway earlier this year,” Caltrans said in a statement. headlines.title: 71-year-old man dies after being struck by self-driving car on I-80 in Vallejo
headlines.description: A 71-year-old man was killed early Thursday morning after he was struck by a self-driving car as he was crossing Interstate 80 in Vallejo, the California Highway Patrol said. According to the CHP’s Solano-area office, officers were alerted to a collision reported around 2:35 a.m. on westbound I-80 at the I-780 interchange. When they arrived, first responders found the severely injured pedestrian, who was later declared dead. The driver of the involved vehicle, a 26-year-old San Francisco man, stayed at the scene and told CHP officers that his vehicle, a Tesla, was being operated in Full Self-Driving autonomous mode when it hit the pedestrian. According to the CHP, the Tesla had full footage of the crash since it was recorded by the vehicle’s dashcam. Based on the video, the Tesla was traveling around 70 mph when the pedestrian entered the freeway. He began crossing toward the center divider from the right shoulder, placing him directly in front of the Tesla. “The video showed the Tesla’s brakes being applied as the vehicle steered to the left in an effort to avoid the pedestrian. Despite these evasive actions, the right front portion of the Tesla struck the individual,” the CHP said in a statement on social media. The agency said the 71-year-old was again struck by at least one more vehicle while lying in the traffic lanes, adding that no other vehicles stopped to cooperate with authorities. The other involved vehicle or driver is yet to be identified. “The Solano Area CHP extends its deepest condolences to the family and friends of the deceased during this difficult time,” the agency said. Anyone who may have witnessed the crash or who has information regarding the other vehicles involved is encouraged to contact the CHP Solano-area office at 707-639-5600.

headlines.title: Video game developer BioWare shuts down, next ‘Mass Effect' canceled amid broader layoffs at EA
headlines.description: Video game publisher Electronic Arts is shutting down the popular and influential game development studio BioWare after more than three decades. The upcoming “Mass Effect” game, the fifth since 2007, has been canceled. BioWare announced the closure on social media Wednesday following a report by Bloomberg that also said the company is laying off 400 people, including about 50 at BioWare. The Redwood Shores, California-based maker of popular titles like “Battlefield” and “The Sims” closed the $55 billion sale of its business to Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund PIF, investment firm Silver Lake Partners and Affinity Partners, which is run by President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, in August. Representatives for EA did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment on the layoffs. “What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember,” the studio said via social media. “These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with characters, and made these worlds your own.” BioWare built its reputation on immersive role-playing adventures, from sword-and-sorcery fantasies like “Baldur’s Gate” and “Dragon Age” to science fiction epics like “Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic” and “Mass Effect.” But its effort to branch out into multiplayer shooters, 2019’s “Anthem,” steered away from the studio’s strength as a creator of compelling single-player narratives. It failed to find the sort of loyal audience that keeps online hits like “Fortnite” and “Overwatch” humming. Meanwhile the latest installments of its two most popular original franchises — 2017’s “Mass Effect: Andromeda” and 2024’s “Dragon Age: The Veilguard” — met with mixed reviews and disappointed many fans. A new chapter of “Mass Effect” was in development before BioWare announced its shutdown. BioWare, based in Canada, was founded in 1995 and acquired by EA in 2007. __ Associated Press Writer Lou Kesten in Washington contributed.
